prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a widely used, single “best” beginner crypto site that also routinely publishes its own trading losses. Most mainstream educational sites teach in plain English but won’t run a public trading P&L because of marketing, legal and regulatory reasons. If you want both clear explanations and real, traceable numbers (including losses), you’ll need to combine a plain-English resource with transparent on‑chain data and/or writers who publish live trade logs.

Here’s a practical approach and a short list of places that meet parts of what you asked for.

What to use for plain-English crypto education
- Coinbase Learn — very beginner-friendly explainers on basic crypto concepts and safety.
- Binance Academy — accessible, structured lessons and glossaries.
- Coin Bureau — long, plain-English guides and videos that explain projects without heavy jargon.
- Bankless — focused on Ethereum/DeFi but written in accessible language (podcasts + newsletters).
- Glassnode Academy — clear explainers of on‑chain metrics (good if you want to learn how real numbers are measured).

Where to see real numbers and (sometimes) losses
- On‑chain explorers and portfolio trackers (for real, verifiable numbers):
  - Etherscan / Solscan / BscScan — see wallet transactions directly.
  - Zapper / Zerion / DeBank — connect a wallet or paste an address to see portfolio P&L, positions and historical transactions.
  - Dune Analytics — community dashboards that show actual on‑chain flows, returns, protocol stats; many dashboards are transparent and reproducible.
- Writers/reporters who publish trade logs or link wallets:
  - Some crypto journalists and independent analysts publish their wallets or Dune dashboards so readers can verify trades and P&L. Look for articles that link to an on‑chain address or a Dune dashboard before trusting claimed returns.

Why you rarely see “publishes losses”
- Marketing & regulatory pressures make most companies and influencers reluctant to post a running, public record of their losses.
- Independent bloggers or traders who are honest about losses do exist, but they’re scattered and often on Twitter/X, substack or personal blogs—look for those who provide a wallet address or dashboard so claims can be verified.

Recommended workflow for a beginner who wants both clarity and transparency
1. Learn the basics in plain English (Coinbase Learn, Coin Bureau, Binance Academy).
2. When you read investment claims, ask: “Do they link a wallet, transaction history, or a Dune dashboard?” If not, treat returns with skepticism.
3. Verify real numbers on-chain (Etherscan) or with portfolio tools (Zapper/Zerion).
4. Follow a few transparent writers who publish trade logs/Dune dashboards; that gives you both narrative and verifiable P&L.

If you want, tell me:
- whether you mean “losses” from educational course authors, newsletter writers, or trading services, and
- whether you care more about spot/long-term investing (BTC/ETH) or DeFi/Trading.

I can then point to specific writers, dashboards or newsletters that publish verifiable trade logs.
